steps: Install the host-built 0.1.24-dev universal module, reboot with the module enabled, and compare the ZIP plus six installed native artifact SHA-256 values
Receive test.txt through Download/localsend-source and test.jpg through Pictures using LocalSend, then verify the payload hashes and unique physical destinations
Read the LocalSend, ExternalStorageProvider and MediaProvider runtime status records and compare domain-specific admission with the actual file results
Force-stop and cold-start LocalSend ten times while checking previous PID cleanup, active/complete/fd_pinned status, three rule mounts, launch telemetry and RSS
Compare runtime status file counts before the retention fix, after reboot, and after ten distinct application PIDs
Stop LocalSend, restart both system Providers, verify new Provider PIDs and active per-action status, then restart LocalSend before and after the Android storage service settles
Force-stop the final LocalSend process and scan every process mountinfo for configured mount residuals while leaving both Providers alive
expected_result: Provider status publication succeeds without post-specialize companion access, per-action Provider admission agrees with LocalSend file placement, dead-PID status history remains bounded, Provider restart fails open during any transient storage gap and recovers after the storage service settles, and application mount namespaces leave no global residual
before_actual: In 0.1.22-dev, LocalSend file placement worked but Provider post-specialize companion access failed with errno 13, no Provider status file was published, and only the aggregate LocalSend mount record existed. In 0.1.23-dev, shared-memory Provider status publication worked, but 26 PID-named status files accumulated after cold starts and Provider restarts because dead PID records had no garbage collection
after_actual: In 0.1.24-dev, both Providers published two active redirect admissions with no missing capability or operation, while LocalSend correctly reported only its mount transaction because this policy has no app-path action. test.txt and test.jpg matched their baseline hashes and existed only under localsend-redirect. Ten cold starts passed 10/10 with one of each configured mount and the status directory stayed at three live-PID files. Restarting both Providers reduced the directory to their two new live records; restarting LocalSend restored it to three and pruned the failed predecessor PID. An immediate application start during storage-service reconstruction reported failed_preflight/ENOENT rather than false active, and a settled retry recovered active/complete/fd_pinned with three mounts. Final force-stop removed the process and all three configured mount residual counts were zero
reviewer_conclusion: The v0.1.24 changes close the observed Provider status transport and dead-PID retention regressions without changing redirect semantics. V-45 active-state agreement, V-48 Provider restart recovery, and the v0.1.24 ten-cycle V-60 supplement are observed on this device with no unexpected regression. The immediate ENOENT is an explicit fail-open storage reconstruction window and recovered on retry; it is not reported as active. Inactive, unsupported, collision, ambiguous and overflow V-45 cases, additional ROM/root/kernel tiers, arm32 execution, and fanotify-dependent scenarios remain outside this single-device report
